name: Hashum
overview: Hashum was a male figure noted in the book of Nehemiah who held a position of honor during the public reading of the Law, standing on Ezra's left hand. While his tribal affiliation is not specified, he is also recognized as one of the signatories on the sealed covenant document in Nehemiah 10. These details place him among the faithful who participated in the religious renewal under Ezra and Nehemiah.
namesAndTitles: The name Hashum means "broad-nosed" and is presented as a proper name without indication that it was divinely given. This straightforward meaning reflects a common Hebrew personal name of the period without additional theological significance.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Hashum beyond what is noted in his public role alongside Ezra. There are no listed relatives or connections beyond his participation in the covenant ceremony and his position during the Law reading.
scriptureSignificance: Hashum's significance lies in his visible support of Ezra's leadership during a pivotal moment of restoring the Law to the people of Israel. His inclusion among the covenant signatories indicates his commitment to the renewed covenant community and the reforms being enacted. Through his participation, Hashum exemplifies the faithful response to God's call for covenant renewal in the post-exilic period.
